title: When Ambition Gets in the Way
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article argues that ambition, though prized and productive when tempered by humility and ethics, becomes a liability when it pulls a leader's attention toward the next role. The author describes how ambition can narrow focus on the future at the expense of the present job. His central claim is that the quality of today's work is a leader's strongest credential, so taking care of the work in front of you must matter as much or more than what lies ahead. Leaders who talk about or investigate their next position too early signal that ambition has taken over, and others stop trusting them. The piece closes with the rule that present performance must always exceed ambition.
points: Ambition fuels achievement but, unbalanced by humility and ethics, can breed aggression and tunnel vision.
Fixation on the next role makes the present role take a back seat, which erodes the quality of current work.
Talking about or scouting the next position before the time has come signals to others that ambition has taken over.
The standard offered is that present performance must always exceed ambition.
quotes: Ambition is a prized quality. It drives people to set and pursue goals on their way to making an impact and leaving a mark.

High ambition can take over our everyday thinking. It can spur aggression that lacks real concern for others. And a more common drawback is how ambition can narrow our focus on the future at the expense of the present.
When ambition directs energy squarely on future aspirations, the present role can take a back seat. Losing focus on the job at hand is a common consequence of unbridled ambition.

Taking care of the work in front of you must always matter as much or more than the work that lies ahead. Ambitious leaders who get ahead of their skis and start planning for the future forget that their strongest credential is the quality of their work today.

Leaders who begin to think about, speak about, and investigate their next role or position before the time has come signal to everyone that their ambition has taken over their sensibilities. We don’t trust leaders or team members who bypass the present so they might gaze upon the stars.

Ambition keeps us in hot pursuit of great outcomes and pushes us to earn a better future. But when future goals become more important than current goals, leaders lose sight as to why they deserve their aspirations to begin with.
